messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@acme-corp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20 09:12 AM -07:00
Subject: Request to delete and export personal data for lucy@acme.com

Hi Rishi and Neha,

We received a formal data subject request from one of our users, lucy@acme.com, asking for a full export of their personal data and for all personal data to be erased from vendors where applicable. Can you confirm Redwood's role (controller vs processor) for data related to Acme account ACME-123 and for model outputs tied to API keys?

Specifically:
- Please provide a data export for lucy@acme.com (including support logs, request metadata, and any cached content).
- Confirm whether Redwood will perform deletion upon our instruction or whether we need to instruct via the DPA process.
- List retention windows and whether there are exemptions for backup logs.

We can provide proof of identity if required — copying Acme Legal for visibility. Targeting to close this within 30 days but prefer an expedited turnaround if possible.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Senior Privacy Counsel
Acme Corp
emma@acme-corp.com

Attachments: n/a (user submitted request via support portal)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20 10:03 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to delete and export personal data for lucy@acme.com

Hi Emma — thanks for the heads-up. We got this and I want to clarify the operational steps so you know what to expect. Short answer: for standard hosted API usage Redwood is a processor and will act on verified controller instructions; we also retain minimal telemetry required for integrity/abuse detection where DPA permits. There are a couple of nuance points below.

Pre-reqs and verification:
- We need a proof-of-identity for the data subject (photo ID redacted is fine). Please ask Lucy to upload to the secure link I'll share in a follow-up.
- Confirm the scope: is this all content tied to the email address (API request logs, support tickets, and any cached prefixes), or do you want us to include aggregated analytics?

Planned steps (operational runbook):
1) Verify identity (Privacy team).
2) Run a scoped export using our DSR tool (dsr-tool export --account ACME-123 --subject lucy@acme.com) to capture request logs, storage objects, and support tickets.
3) Legal/Privacy to confirm any retention exemptions (e.g., fraud logs).
4) On controller instruction, perform deletion for provider-managed objects and confirm with an audit log.

SLA: standard DPA window is 30 days; we will attempt to complete the export & deletion within 5 business days after verification for this case. I have copied Neha (privacy) to begin verification and Marissa (legal) if there's any contractual nuance.

Attachments: I'll attach the redacted identity upload link once provided.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Request to delete and export personal data for lucy@acme.com (internal)

Thanks — looping in legal and ops playbooks. Quick internal checklist and assignments: 

- Neha (privacy): I will verify identity via the secure intake link and validate the scope. Expecting proof_of_id_redacted.pdf from Acme.
- Rishi (sales): please confirm with Acme whether model outputs generated by customer prompts are considered part of the export scope — they usually are controller-managed content.
- Marissa (legal): please confirm if backup retention exemptions apply under our DPA (we generally retain encrypted backups for 90 days, with limited access). If exemptions apply, we need to document legal basis.
- Ops: run dsr-tool export --account ACME-123 --subject lucy@acme.com and produce dsr-audit-20260520.log. After verification and controller instruction, run dsr-tool delete --scope subject --confirm --audit dsr-audit-20260520.log

Notes:
- For hosted API: Redwood = processor. For Redwood Console support ticket notes we store minimal business metadata and may act as controller for account-specific billing contact info — will flag if any of that needs separate handling.
- If Acme asks us to act without an explicit instruction, we'll request a signed controller directive per Section 4.2 of the DPA.

Attaching the DPA extract for reference (dpa_section-processor-controller-extract.pdf) and linking the internal runbook. I'll start verification once the proof of ID is in.

— Neha Kapoor
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Emma — quick update and confirmation.

Summary of actions taken:
- We received a redacted ID (proof_of_id_redacted.pdf) and validated the requestor via Acme Legal.
- Privacy ran the export: dsr-tool export --account ACME-123 --subject lucy@acme.com — produced dsr-audit-20260520.log (attached).
- Legal reviewed retention windows per DPA and confirmed no legal hold applies. See attached DPA extract for the controller/processor mapping.
- On controller instruction (Acme confirmed by reply), we performed deletion of subject-scoped storage objects and removed request logs from hot stores. Encrypted backups will expire per our standard retention policy (90 days) — backups are immutable for integrity and cannot be truncated immediately; we documented this in dsr-audit-20260520.log.

What we removed: API request bodies, support ticket content, and account-linked metadata for lucy@acme.com from active storage. What remains: encrypted backups (retention window), aggregated analytics (non-identifiable).

Attachments: dsr-audit-20260520.log, dpa_section-processor-controller-extract.pdf

If you need a signed confirmation on company letterhead or an export in a specific format (CSV vs JSONL), let us know. Thank you for the clear scope — closing this ticket unless you ask for further follow-up.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
